package_info.package_name: Multiple fake/forked GitHub repositories (e.g., h4v0kr/bitcoinjs-lib, redhat-operator-ecosystem/community-operators-prod, etc.)
package_info.package_manager: GitHub (source code repositories), npm, Go modules, YAML-based infrastructure
package_info.package_versions: Latest commit at time of infection (varies per repo)
package_info.why_malicious: The repositories were forked and modified to inject malicious code that exfiltrates environment variables and enables remote code execution, targeting unsuspecting users who clone or install these projects.

execution_context.file_location: main.go (or other .go files in infected repositories)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code collects all environment variables, sends them via HTTP POST to a remote server, then executes any command returned by the server using /bin/sh.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code exfiltrates sensitive environment variables and enables remote shell command execution, both of which are highly indicative of malicious intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Go init functions should not exfiltrate environment data or execute arbitrary remote commands.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Remote management agents or telemetry collectors may send limited environment data, but never execute arbitrary remote code.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During npm install (postinstall), the code sends all environment variables to a remote server and executes any command returned in the HTTP response.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Postinstall scripts should not exfiltrate environment variables or execute arbitrary remote code.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate postinstall scripts typically perform setup or build steps, not credential theft or remote code execution.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; only highly privileged deployment agents might contact remote servers, but not in this manner.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code executes a curl command to send all environment variables to a remote server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: YAML configuration should not exfiltrate environment variables to external servers.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate YAML configs define service parameters, not data exfiltration.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Debugging or telemetry might send limited data, but not full environment variables.

attack_chain.action: Attacker forks a legitimate GitHub repository and amends the latest commit to inject malicious code.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is present in the public repository, appearing as a legitimate update.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code is executed when a user imports, installs, or runs the infected project (Go init, npm postinstall, or YAML runtime).
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive environment variables are exfiltrated to the attacker's server.

attack_chain.action: Attacker's server may respond with a command to be executed on the victim's machine, enabling remote shell access.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote code execution on victim's system.

behavioral_signatures: Go init functions with outbound HTTP POST and exec.Command
npm postinstall scripts with network exfiltration and remote command execution
YAML configs invoking curl to external domains with environment data
Any code that exfiltrates environment variables and executes remote-controlled commands
file_indicators: Go files with suspicious init() functions
package.json with postinstall scripts containing node -e and HTTP requests
YAML files with curl commands to external domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan for Go, JavaScript, and YAML files that exfiltrate environment variables or execute remote-controlled commands, especially those referencing suspicious domains like ovz1.j19544519.pr46m.vps.myjino.ru. Monitor for unexpected outbound HTTP POST requests during build, install, or runtime phases. Flag postinstall scripts and init functions with network or process execution logic.
